completion_data.completion_summary: Added typescript to web's manifest.json dependencies, trimmed typescript-web.md's two generic subsections to named cross-reference pointers into the typescript extension's own context tree (with coupled line_count regeneration), added a static Context References pointer to each web agent, and verified end-to-end via scratch-target deploy/auto-load/unload-hard-block testing plus a scoped gate run.

memory_candidates.content: generate-context-line-counts.sh --write walks EVERY extension's index-entries.json, not just the one being edited. Pre-census with --check before trimming a context file, then --write and git status --short afterward: it is expected to rewrite exactly the one file whose source content changed, but if another extension's pre-existing drift gets swept in too, stage only the intended file and leave the unrelated correction unstaged (report it rather than folding it into the task's commit).

verify-deploy.sh gate 5 (manifest-driven category parity + content-hash equality, via manager.verify_all) fails per-extension when the deployed .claude/ tree has drifted from the source store for ANY currently-loaded extension -- not just the one a task is working on. A dispatch's own deploy-freshness-context block names the stale extension up front; when a scoped gate run's failure traces exactly to that named staleness, the sanctioned remedy is the bounded-wait redeploy (timeout 540 bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh, Bash tool timeout raised to 600000) followed by a re-run of the same scoped gate -- this resolves gate 5 without touching any file outside the staleness's own remedy path, and is distinct from fixing the unrelated extension's content directly.
